name: enshrouded
about: Enshrouded's melee (Keen Games, Steam app 1203620), the developers' measuring stick for combat (D180), measured frame by frame from first-party video. Round 1 (2026-10-24): the heavy blow, a parried enemy blow and the camera's framing. Round 2 (2026-10-24): the light chain, the roll's timing, a landed blow's hit-stop and the spacing; what these sources cannot show is listed under `unmeasured`. `targets` gives the ranges our set and camera should land in. research/2026-10-24-enshrouded-combat-measured.md says how and compares our move set.

units.time: seconds of game time (the videos play at 1x)
units.length: body heights (one body: the player's standing height on screen, about 1.8 m)

ftp.title: Enshrouded - Forging the Path | Combat (Keen's developers on Update 8's combat, with gameplay inserts)
ftp.frames: 1920x900 at 60 fps, every frame read at 0.5x (about one in three dropped)
ftp.build: Update 8, the current melee (charged heavy, i-frames on the roll, warping to targets)

cg.title: Enshrouded - Combat Gameplay
cg.frames: 1920x1080 at 60 fps (about one frame in ten a repeat), every frame read at 0.25x
cg.build: pre-release 2023; melee reworked since (Update 8), so its timings are older than the game's

steam.note: the store's two trailers (1.0 launch, Wake of the Water) are cinematic cuts with almost no readable melee; used only to confirm that

method: Frames caught from the official videos in a headless Chromium (each frame's media time from requestVideoFrameCallback), laid out as labelled contact sheets and read by eye: a phase starts on the first frame the pose leaves the last one. Distances are on-screen body heights; camera distance is derived from the player's share of the frame height for an assumed vertical field of view (Enshrouded's is a slider whose default is not published). Pictures are kept in ~/.cache/terra-review/refs/enshrouded-combat/, never in the repository.

heavy.what: Update 8's sword heavy (one-handed sword, round shield on the left arm) on a training dummy: a crouched turn and draw-back while the button is held, a short leap, an overhead cut, a bent-over landing, back to guard
heavy.windup_note: from the first frame leaving idle (51.95) to the impact flash (52.47); includes however long the button was held, so it is the shortest charge shown, not a fixed wind-up
heavy.lunge_note: the leap carries the body toward the dummy; read from the body's change of size on screen, so a range
heavy.confidence: medium on times (±0.03 s), low on the lunge

light_chain.what: Update 8's sword-and-shield light blows on a golden training dummy, the 'After Update 8' half of the warp comparison, seen from the gameplay camera behind: four blows from idle, the first three out of reach (the warp no longer closes the gap), the fourth stepping in and landing with a flash, then bent over and back to guard
light_chain.idle_to_hit_note: idle held 244.73-244.95, first frame leaving it 244.967 (sword raised), the blade's trail from 245.20 to 245.32, mid-sweep 245.25
light_chain.hit_to_settled_note: after blows 1 to 3 the follow-through stops by about 0.2 s after the hit and the sword is held out ahead (frame-to-frame motion near zero) until the next blow's wind-up; none of them returns to guard, so a light blow's own recovery to guard is not shown
light_chain.hit_to_hit_note: 0.75, 0.92 and 0.73-0.80 s between hits (mid-sweep, or the flash for the fourth); the sword is held still between blows, so this is the player's pace, an upper bound on the chain's cadence, not its shortest
light_chain.blows_note: the chain runs at least four; the fourth steps in (a lunge of a few tenths of a body height), lands, and ends bent over like the heavy; whether a fifth follows is not shown
light_chain.last_hit_to_guard_note: flash 247.72, bent over with the sword down until about 248.15, rising and turning the shield to 248.53, on guard by 248.77
light_chain.method: every frame (captured slowed; 339 of 348 gaps one frame), contact sheets of the player cropped, and frame-to-frame motion over the player (motion.mjs)
light_chain.confidence: medium on the first blow's wind-up and the last blow's recovery (±0.03 s); low on the cadence as a design value (player-paced); one chain only

roll.what: Update 8's dodge roll (a greatsword player against a torch-and-axe humanoid, a free cinematic camera), narrated 'we also added i-frames to the dodge roll' and 'the dodge roll will have the i-frames and will not roll around enemies by default'
roll.duration_note: first frame leaving the stand to standing again: 155.85-156.38 and 156.48-157.00 s; dive about 0.2 s, tucked ball about 0.1 s, kneel and rise about 0.2 s
roll.roll_to_roll_note: rolls chained back to back start at 155.85, 156.48, 157.12 and 157.70 s; the third rises straight into a raised-sword attack
roll.distance_note: not measurable: the camera turns and tracks with the player through every roll shown, and the enemy, the only ruler, is at another depth
roll.iframes: present by Keen's word; nothing on screen marks them (no flash, no tint), so their window is not measurable from video
roll.method: frames captured slowed (about one gap in fourteen two frames or more), contact sheets of the player cropped
roll.confidence: medium on the duration (±0.03 s, two rolls agree); medium on the chained cadence (three intervals)

enemy_overhead_parried.what: a cave scavenger's overhead axe blow taken on a raised shield and parried (a white burst on the shield), 2023 build
enemy_overhead_parried.windup_note: axe rising from 22.50 to its top at about 22.95, falling to the burst at 23.30; the video cuts on the next frame

camera.player_across_frame: centred (within about 5% of the middle) in every Update 8 combat shot; no shoulder offset shows
camera.distance_note: d = 1 body / (2 * share * tan(vfov/2)); share 0.20 to 0.27. If the 1920x900 picture is a 1080-high frame cropped, the share against the full frame is about a sixth smaller and the camera that much further
camera.height: a little above the head, looking slightly down: the horizon sits in the upper third, the player's feet in the lower third
camera.in_a_fight: pulls no closer for a fight; the enemy is framed ahead of the player, both in view, the player low and centred; the merciless finisher (2023) cuts to a close side camera
camera.older_2023_camera: much closer, over the right shoulder, the player cut at the waist (cg 20-50 s)
camera.confidence: medium on the share and centring, low on the distance (field of view unknown)

guard.what: Update 8's idle with sword and shield: the round shield on the left forearm held in front of the chest and belly, face toward the enemy, sword low in the right hand along the leg, point down and back; the 2023 block holds a rectangular shield up to the face, sword low

hit_stop.what: the light chain's fourth blow landing on the training dummy (Update 8)
hit_stop.note: every frame from 247.60 to 247.95 s was caught; over the player's legs, clear of the flash, each frame differs from the last by 7 to 30 (of 255) through the contact, so the body is not held for even one frame; the camera kicks over the same frames (the sky moves 3 to 8 from 247.67 to 247.77, still before and after). The flash runs 247.717-247.767. A held pose of one frame hidden by the camera's kick cannot be ruled out; anything longer would show
hit_stop.method: frame-to-frame difference in a crop of the legs and of the sky (motion.mjs) and a contact sheet of every frame
hit_stop.confidence: medium for this blow on a dummy; one landed hit; a hit on a living enemy, or a heavy, may hold differently and none is shown at a usable frame rate

spacing.note: a greatsword player trading with a torch-and-axe humanoid, read where both stand at about the same depth (feet level in the frame): 0.75 at 178.2 s, about 0.5 at 176.7 and 177.0 s, about 1.3 enemy heights mid-dodge at 155.83 s. On the dummy the light blows whiff at a stand-off the camera cannot measure from behind, and the fourth steps in to land with the shield almost touching it
spacing.method: horizontal gap between the two bodies' middles over the player's standing height on screen, in single frames
spacing.confidence: low: across the view only (depth unknown, so a lower bound where they are not side by side), a two-handed weapon, a free camera

targets.about: the ranges our sword-and-shield set and camera should land in, from these numbers; real seconds

unmeasured.block_raise_and_blocked_hit: no block in Update 8's official footage (none in the inserts of RDQ0_R4AR-A read so far); cg 20-51 s holds the 2023 block held, not its raise
unmeasured.roll_distance_and_iframes: the rolls shown are under a camera that tracks the player, and i-frames are not drawn; needs a fixed-camera roll (third-party footage) and cannot come from video for the i-frames
unmeasured.light_recovery_to_guard: every light blow shown is followed by the next; a lone light blow back to guard is not in Keen's videos
unmeasured.shortest_chain_cadence: the chain shown is player-paced; the shortest needs a mashed chain (third-party footage)
unmeasured.hit_stop_on_enemies: the only landed blow caught without drops is on a dummy; the 2023 video repeats frames
unmeasured.hit_reaction: the cave scavenger's stagger rings (cg 36.5-41.5 s) show a stun of about 5 s, not a flinch; flinch lengths not read
unmeasured.not_looked_at: Keen's highlights video ToMwQsJTaEM, and RDQ0_R4AR-A 93-104 s (a camp fight with weapon skills)
